label: December 2026
intro: December is when most of us set next year's plan. This month's four reads come at the same question from different angles: is the company you're building ready for what's next, and are you?
Start with the AI piece. Then forward the leadership one to someone on your team and ask what it would mean for you.

picks.author: Joseph Esteves
picks.title: The Biggest AI Risk Is Automating The Wrong Company
picks.summary: Counting AI licenses and training completions tells you nothing about value. Esteves says the payoff comes from questioning why a process exists before you automate it, then aiming AI at revenue, responsiveness and capacity with clear owners.

picks.author: Alec Litowitz
picks.title: AQ Is A Learnable Discipline. Here Are Four Places CEOs Can Start
picks.summary: The leaders who win over time are the most adaptable, not the smartest, and adaptability can be trained. Four starting points: anchor your identity in adapting instead of being right, test before committing, and set up your team to surface early warning signs and protect dissenters.

picks.author: Ajay Tejasvi
picks.title: The last test of leadership
picks.summary: The habits that built your company can become the thing holding it back. Tejasvi suggests asking regularly what the business needs now, whether you're still the right person to provide it, and building successors and systems that don't depend on you.

picks.author: Sean Hackbarth
picks.title: Small Businesses Have Momentum. Here's How to Make It Last.
picks.summary: Owners at the Chamber's CO-100 forum were upbeat despite inflation and labor shortages. Their advice: be upfront with customers about costs, plan backward from a long-term goal, and describe what you sell specifically enough that AI search can find you.
